architectural_decisions.title: MFE + BFF Architecture Pattern
architectural_decisions.decision: React Vite micro-frontends with Spring Boot Backend for Frontend
architectural_decisions.rationale: Separation of concerns between frontend teams, independent deployment, BFF provides unified API facade for MFEs
implications: Frontend teams can work independently on MFEs
BFF handles cross-cutting concerns (auth, rate limiting, aggregation)

architectural_decisions.title: Offline-First Data Sync
architectural_decisions.decision: Local PouchDB with custom sync protocol to PostgreSQL backend
architectural_decisions.rationale: Field operations require reliable offline capability with conflict resolution
implications: PouchDB in browser for local persistence
Custom sync protocol for conflict detection

architectural_decisions.title: Netlify for Frontend Hosting
architectural_decisions.decision: Netlify for MFE hosting with Netlify Functions for serverless backend
architectural_decisions.rationale: Simple deployment, built-in CI/CD, serverless functions for lightweight backend
constraints: Functions timeout at 10s — use async processing for long tasks
Connection pooling: max 20 connections per function instance

architectural_decisions.title: Multi-Tenant Data Isolation
architectural_decisions.decision: Row-level security (RLS) in PostgreSQL with tenant_id column
architectural_decisions.rationale: Cost-effective, maintains single codebase, RLS provides defense in depth
implications: All tables must have tenant_id column
RLS policies on all tenant-scoped tables
Application must set tenant context on connection

technical_learnings.learning: Netlify Functions timeout at 10 seconds — use async processing for long tasks
technical_learnings.context: Barcode scanning and image processing exceed timeout
technical_learnings.solution: Offload to background job with webhook callback

technical_learnings.learning: Connection pooling: max 20 connections per Netlify Function instance
technical_learnings.solution: Use PgBouncer or connection pooler, limit concurrent connections

technical_learnings.learning: PouchDB replication conflicts on high-write scenarios
technical_learnings.solution: Implement last-write-wins with vector clocks for conflict resolution

technical_learnings.learning: MFE shared dependencies must be externalized to avoid duplication
technical_learnings.context: Bundle size explosion with multiple MFEs
technical_learnings.solution: Use module federation with shared dependencies configured

patterns_and_conventions.name: BFF Aggregation Pattern
patterns_and_conventions.description: BFF aggregates multiple backend services into unified frontend API
patterns_and_conventions.example: Catalog BFF aggregates product, pricing, and inventory services

patterns_and_conventions.name: Offline Queue Pattern
patterns_and_conventions.description: Queue mutations locally when offline, sync when online
patterns_and_conventions.example: Scan results queued in PouchDB, synced to PostgreSQL on reconnect

patterns_and_conventions.name: Tenant Context Pattern
patterns_and_conventions.description: Tenant ID propagated through all layers via context/middleware
patterns_and_conventions.example: JWT contains tenant_id, middleware sets PostgreSQL session variable

active_constraints: PostgreSQL: 20 connections per function instance max
PouchDB: 50MB local storage limit per origin
